answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents stake tokens into a trust graph where multi-agent auditing evaluates topological cut verifications. If collusion creates an echo of false attestations, cross-cluster auditors verify edge sparsity; detecting a fraudulent cut triggers immediate stake slashing, reducing the attacker's capital to an ember. Because validating across honest cuts scales auditing bonds superlinearly, reaching an adversarial zenith requires superlinear capital costs that make sustained infiltration mathematically unviable.
